    StartersPorpoise Spit prawn cocktailPrawns on shredded iceberg with creamy tomato cocktail sauceHow to make it500g cooked king prawns120g mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp Worcestershire sauce1 tsp hot sauce1/2 iceberg lettuce2 lemonsPeel the prawns, keeping them chilled.Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce and a squeeze of lemon.Shred the lettuce into four glasses, pile on the prawns and spoon over the sauce. Hang a lemon wedge on each rim.Chicken tarragon vol-au-ventsPuff pastry cases filled with creamy chicken, mushroom and tarragonHow to make it2 sheets of puff pastry250g chicken thigh fillets150g mushrooms20g butter200ml thickened cream1 tbsp chopped tarragon1 lemonThaw the pastry. Cut 16 rounds, press a smaller cutter into each, and place on trays.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden, then push the centres down.Dice the chicken and chop the mushrooms. Fry both in the butter until cooked.Add the cream, tarragon and a squeeze of lemon and simmer until thick.Fill the cases and warm through in the oven.Hibiscus Island tropical fruit platterThe island holiday with RhondaHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pineapple, mango, papaya and lychees on crushed ice with lime cheeks, a chilli lime salt and a passionfruit and coconut yoghurt dip.Peel and cut 1 pineapple and 2 mangoes into wedges, slice half a papaya and peel 250g lychees.Arrange over a tray of crushed ice with 2 limes cut into cheeks.Mix 1 tbsp sea salt with half a tsp chilli powder and the zest of 1 lime.Stir the pulp of 3 passionfruit into 200g coconut yoghurt with 1 tbsp honey.Serve the salt and dip on the side.Fairy bread trianglesWaterloo playing, Rhonda on the microphone.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsSweet and sour pork with riceCrispy pork in a sweet and sour sauce with capsicum and pineappleHow to make it600g pork shoulder1 tbsp soy sauce90g cornflour1 red capsicum200g pineapple pieces3 tbsp white vinegar3 tbsp caster sugar4 tbsp tomato sauce100ml water400g jasmine rice1 L vegetable oilCube the pork, toss with the soy sauce, then coat in most of the cornflour. Slice the capsicum.Cook the rice by the absorption method and keep warm.Fry the pork in batches in oil at 180°C until crisp, then drain.Stir fry the capsicum and pineapple in a wok, add the vinegar, sugar, tomato sauce and water, and thicken with the last of the cornflour mixed with a little water.Toss the pork through the sauce and serve with the rice.Van Arkle wedding alternate dropThe alternate drop at the wedding that paid $10,000How to make itAs written, serves 4Every second guest gets chicken breast in creamy mushroom sauce, the rest get eye fillet with red wine jus, both with dauphinoise and green beans.Layer 1kg thinly sliced potatoes with 300ml cream, garlic and salt and bake at 180°C for 60 minutes.Sear 2 chicken breasts and 2 eye fillet steaks.Roast the chicken at 200°C for 15 minutes and the beef 8 minutes, then rest.In one pan cook 200g mushrooms, add 150ml cream.In another reduce 125ml red wine with 200ml beef stock.Steam 300g green beans.Plate alternately.SweetsMariel's wedding cakeVanilla cake with raspberry jam and buttercream under white fondantHow to make it400g butter250g caster sugar4 eggs300g self-raising flour125ml full cream milk150g raspberry jam300g icing sugar500g white fondant1 punnet of fresh edible flowers, to decorateBeat 250g of the butter with the caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs. Fold in the flour and milk.Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake at 165°C.Cool the cakes completely in the tins and on a rack.Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar for the buttercream.Sandwich the cakes with jam and buttercream, coat thinly with buttercream, then cover with rolled fondant.Decorate with fresh flowers and serve in fingers.DrinksHibiscus Island piña coladaFrozen blended rum, pineapple and coconut cream with a paper umbrellaHow to make it180ml white rum250ml pineapple juice150ml coconut cream60ml lime juice1 tbsp sugar syrup4 cups ice1 small pineapple4 cocktail cherries4 paper umbrellasCut the pineapple into wedges for garnish.Blend the rum, pineapple juice, coconut cream, lime juice, syrup and ice until thick and smooth.Pour into four tall glasses and garnish with a pineapple wedge, a cherry and a paper umbrella. Swap the rum for extra pineapple juice to make it alcohol-free.
